title: Kernel affinity drift containment and benchmarking
creator: Aisha Nguyen
description: Summary: After the scheduler path-probing heuristic rollout on 2026-02-22 we observed a persistent p95 latency increase (20–45%) for multi-turn chat, correlated with a shift in kernel affinity for medium-length sequences (512–1024 tokens). The incident caused intermittent tail-latency spikes and ~12% sustained throughput drop on affected pools. This ticket contains containment actions, a reproducible benchmark suite, and longer-term hardening deliverables to prevent kernel affinity drift and its downstream KV-cache amplification effects.

root_cause: The scheduler-probe-v3 change broadened the probing window to evaluate candidate kernels more aggressively. Under mixed workloads the revised probe ordering interacted poorly with the kernel-ranking score function: small timing differences pushed a subset of requests to less-optimized kernels. Those kernels had different KV-cache warming characteristics, causing higher miss rates and amplifying latency impact through downstream KV miss amplification. Contributing factors: insufficient deterministic kernel ranking for tie-breaks, lack of synthetic workload coverage for 512–1024 token multi-turn patterns, and canary windows that were too short for cache-warm behaviors to surface.
mitigation: Immediate: rollback scheduler-probe-v3 (done), pinned affected pools to stable kernel-ranking snapshot, increased canary observation window to 6 hours. Short-term: introduce a deterministic tie-breaker in kernel ranking, add a KV-cache miss metric to the canary health checks, and expand synthetic benchmark suite to include multi-turn 512–1024 token patterns. Long-term: implement a kernel-ranking monotonicity guard (reject changes that increase entropy beyond threshold), add automated replay gating before rollouts, and surface per-kernel kv_hit_rate in the Console.
